mainTopic: רבי אליעזר's sources for why the מכשירין of ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת, while those of לולב, סוכה, מצה, שופר and מילה do
overview: The amud opens by rejecting an earlier reason why, for רבי אליעזר, the preparations (מכשירין) of ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת. The new reason is that a person can always make the garment or house הפקר and avoid the obligation. Next the גמרא goes through a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר says that the מכשירין of לולב, סוכה, מצה, שופר and מילה override שבת, and it asks for his source for each one. לולב comes from ״ביום״, which means even on שבת. סוכה is learned from לולב through the גזירה שוה ״שבעת ימים״, and מצה is learned from סוכות through ״חמשה עשר״. שופר comes from ״יום תרועה״. Along the way the גמרא shows how the רבנן read the same words as 'by day, not by night,' and where רבי אליעזר learns that daytime rule instead. Each time it asks why the תורה did not write the rule in one place only. The answer is always that each מצוה has a special feature that blocks the comparison: צורך גבוה, four species, night as well as day, applying to women, or the unique power of the שופר. The amud ends as the גמרא begins searching for רבי אליעזר's source for מילה, and that search continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Every moment is the time for these מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the earlier claim that ציצית and מזוזה have no fixed time. Their time is every moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not so that every single moment is its time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges an earlier explanation. That explanation said the preparations for ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת because these מצוות have no set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said that 'no fixed time' means there is no urgency. The challenge turns this around: ציצית and מזוזה apply all the time, so every moment is a moment of obligation. If so, there is constant urgency, and that reason cannot explain why their מכשירין are not allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a moment / an hour
its time (its proper time for the מצוה)
preparations that make a מצוה possible

phrases.english: Every single moment
phrases.notes: Refers to ציצית and מזוזה, discussed on the previous amud.

phrases.english: is its time!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given on the previous amud ('they have no fixed time').
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ציצית and מזוזה have no fixed time, so their preparations do not override שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצוה that applies at every moment is the most constant obligation there is. Having 'no fixed time' does not make it less pressing.

steps.title: A person can always make the items ownerless
steps.stepSummary: New reason: since a person can make his garment or house הפקר and escape the obligation, the preparations do not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said in the name of רבי יצחק (and some say it was רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע): since he has the power to make them ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old reason and gives a new one. These preparations do not override שבת because the person can avoid the obligation entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation of ציצית depends on owning a four-cornered garment, and מזוזה depends on owning a house. A person could make the garment or house הפקר and then have no obligation. A מצוה you can lawfully get out of is not pressing enough to override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: since / because
to make them ownerless (הֶפְקֵר)
and some say (introduces another possible speaker)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, the preparations for ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת. The reason is not about timing. It is that the obligation can be avoided by making the item הפקר.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
since it is in his power to make them ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason rejected in step 1 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement reasoning (אלא): a different reason is given.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the reason was that these מצוות have no fixed time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real reason is that the obligation can be avoided by making the object הפקר, so it lacks the force to override שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: לולב and its preparations override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר says לולב and all its preparations override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: לולב and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about לולב so that it can analyze it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'all its preparations' is the key point. It is not only taking the לולב that is allowed on שבת. Even preparation work, such as cutting it from the tree or carrying it, is allowed on the first day when that day falls on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master said (introduces a quote from a ברייתא)
palm branch taken on סוכות
override שבת

phrases.english: The Master said:
The lulav and all its preparations
override Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion of the ברייתא's ruling on לולב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, לולב and all its preparations override שבת.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אליעזר learns this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רבי אליעזר learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's ruling. This sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Overriding שבת is a major step, so it needs a clear source. The גמרא will first test one possible source and then give the real one.

keyTerms.meaning: from where does he learn it?

phrases.english: From where does Rabbi Eliezer derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the preparations for לולב override שבת.

steps.title: עומר and שתי הלחם cannot be the source
steps.stepSummary: The עומר and שתי הלחם cannot serve as a source, because they are needs of the Temple service (צורך גבוה).
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he learns it from the עומר and the שתי הלחם, that will not work: those are a need of the Most High!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible source and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The preparations for the עומר and שתי הלחם do override שבת. But those are offerings in the מקדש, which serve God directly (צורך גבוה). לולב is a personal מצוה, so a rule about Temple needs cannot be applied to it.

keyTerms.meaning: barley offering brought on the 16th of Nissan
the two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
a need of the Most High (Temple service)

phrases.english: If from the omer and the two loaves,
that is different, since they are a need of the Most High!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מֵעוֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, שֶׁכֵּן צוֹרֶךְ גָּבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one candidate source for the question in step 4 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the עומר and שתי הלחם as a source for לולב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those cases are צורך גבוה (Temple service), which has a stronger power to override שבת than a personal מצוה like לולב.

steps.title: The source is the word 'on the day'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״ביום״, meaning the לולב is taken on the first day even when it is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says: ״ביום״, 'on the day.' 'On the day' means even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אליעזר's real source: the word ״ביום״ in the פסוק about לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא כג:מ) says to take the four species ״ביום הראשון״. רבי אליעזר reads ״ביום״ as saying 'on that day, no matter what,' even if it is שבת. This shows that the מצוה is tied to the day strongly enough to override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק says
on the day
even on שבת

phrases.english: Rather, the verse states: 'On the day.'
'On the day' means even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real source after the rejection in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״ביום״ teaches that the מצוה of לולב applies even on שבת.

steps.title: What does 'on the day' come to permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific שבת rule ״ביום״ comes to override.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what הלכה is it needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly the פסוק permits on שבת. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply picking up the לולב and shaking it involves no מלאכה. So the גמרא wants to know which prohibition the פסוק needed to override.

keyTerms.meaning: for what halacha?

phrases.english: And for what halacha is this needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the derivation in step 6 actually permits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which שבת prohibition the word ״ביום״ comes to override.

steps.title: Not needed just to permit moving the לולב
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק cannot be coming only to permit טלטול, since that would not need a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it permits moving the לולב: would a פסוק be needed to permit moving it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the פסוק permits moving the לולב and rejects that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on moving מוקצה items (טלטול) is only מדרבנן. The תורה would not need a פסוק to permit something that only the חכמים prohibited. So ״ביום״ must be overriding something more serious.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say
moving an object (here, a מוקצה issue)
is it needed?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying moving a לולב is forbidden. It is saying that טלטול is too minor a matter (only מדרבנן) for the תורה to need a פסוק to permit it.

phrases.english: If you say it is to permit moving it,
is a verse needed to permit moving?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one answer to the question in step 7 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects טלטול as the purpose of ״ביום״.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: טלטול is only a rabbinic prohibition, so a פסוק is not needed to permit it.

steps.title: The פסוק permits the לולב's preparations
steps.stepSummary: ״ביום״ comes to permit the מכשירין of the לולב on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for its preparations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the פסוק permits real מלאכה done to prepare the לולב on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since moving the לולב did not need a פסוק, the פסוק must be permitting actual Torah-level מלאכות, like cutting or carrying the לולב. This matches the ברייתא's wording, 'all its preparations.'

keyTerms.meaning: its preparations

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, ״ביום״ teaches that even Torah-level preparation work for the לולב is permitted on the first day of סוכות when it falls on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, it is for its preparations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 after step 8 ruled out טלטול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״ביום״ permits the מכשירי לולב on שבת, according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read 'on the day'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר, so what do they learn from ״ביום״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree, use the word ״ביום״. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן do not allow the מכשירין on שבת, the word ״ביום״ must teach them something else. Otherwise it would seem extra.

keyTerms.meaning: and the Rabbis (what do they say?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the opposing view on the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן use the word ״ביום״.

steps.title: By day, not by night
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״ביום״ to teach that לולב must be taken by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that word to teach: by day and not by night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the רבנן learn a timing rule from ״ביום״, not a שבת rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, ״ביום״ means 'during the daytime,' which excludes the night. So they have no extra word to teach that the מכשירין override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different teaching)
and not at night

steps.whatToRemember: The same word ״ביום״ is read two ways. רבי אליעזר reads it as 'even on שבת'; the רבנן read it as 'by day, not by night.'

phrases.english: That word is needed by them
to teach: by day and not by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use ״ביום״ to limit the מצוה of לולב to daytime.

steps.title: How does רבי אליעזר know לולב is only by day?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי אליעזר uses ״ביום״ to permit the מכשירין on שבת, the גמרא asks where he learns that לולב is taken by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר: where does he learn that the מצוה is by day and not at night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי אליעזר gets the rule that לולב is taken only by day. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, the רבנן used ״ביום״ to teach the daytime rule. רבי אליעזר already used ״ביום״ for the מכשירין on שבת (Step 9), so he needs a different source for the daytime rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?
By day and not at night

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
by day and not at night, from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the רבנן's use of ״ביום״ back onto רבי אליעזר: what is his source for the same rule?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי אליעזר's source for the rule that לולב is taken by day only

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns it from ״ושמחתם... שבעת ימים״
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns the daytime rule from the פסוק ״ושמחתם לפני ה׳ אלקיכם שבעת ימים״, which says days and not nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "And you shall rejoice before ה׳ your God seven days." It says days, and not nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר learns the daytime rule from a different פסוק that says "seven days."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״ימים״ (days) is read precisely to mean daytime only. This frees ״ביום״ for רבי אליעזר's other teaching about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
And you shall rejoice (the פסוק about לולב in ויקרא)
Days and not nights

phrases.english: He derives it from "And you shall rejoice
before the Lord your God seven days"
days, and not nights.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם שִׁבְעַת יָמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר learns the daytime rule from ״שבעת ימים״, meaning days and not nights.

steps.title: Why the רבנן still need ״ביום״
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need ״ביום״ anyway. Without it, we might compare the ״שבעת ימים״ of לולב to the ״שבעת ימים״ of סוכה, which applies at night too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? It was needed. You might have thought we should learn "seven days" from סוכה: just as there it means days and even nights, so too here it means days and even nights. So ״ביום״ teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with the ״ימים ולא לילות״ argument, and answers right away. ״שבעת ימים״ alone would not be enough, so ״ביום״ is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכה also says "seven days," yet you sit in the סוכה at night too. Because of this, we might have read "seven days" by לולב the same way, to include nights. ״ביום״ blocks that comparison and makes clear that לולב is daytime only.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
You might have thought to say
Let us derive
Just as there... so too here
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison to סוכה is the 'you might have thought' (הוה אמינא). It is rejected. The final rule is that לולב is only by day.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: An implied question: why do the רבנן need ״ביום״ if ״ימים״ already teaches this?

phrases.english: It was necessary,
for it might have entered your mind to say
let us derive "seven days" from sukka:
just as there it means days and even nights,
so too here, days and even nights —
therefore it teaches us (that it is only by day).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן's need for ״ביום״ against רבי אליעזר's alternative source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״שבעת ימים״ alone could have been compared to סוכה, which includes nights. So ״ביום״ is needed to say daytime only.

steps.title: Why not write it once, with לולב, and learn the rest from it?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אליעזר, the גמרא challenges: the Torah should have written the rule only by לולב, and the other cases could learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write it with לולב, and let these other cases come and learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for a separate source for each case. If one mention could teach the rule, why does the Torah repeat it in other places too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר and שתי הלחם already have their own source showing that their מכשירין override שבת, and now לולב has its own source in ״ביום״. The תורה does not write extra teachings for nothing. So why not write the rule only by לולב, and let the עומר and שתי הלחם learn from it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah write
And let these come
And let them learn from it

phrases.english: And let the Torah write it with regard to lulav,
and let these others come and learn from it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּלוּלָב, וְנֵיתוֹ הָנָךְ וְנֵילְפוּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the daytime question to whether a separate source for each case is wasteful.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate source for the עומר and שתי הלחם, when לולב's ״ביום״ could have taught them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One mention, by לולב, should be enough for the others to learn from, so the extra mentions seem unnecessary.

steps.title: לולב is special: it needs four species
steps.stepSummary: We could not learn the other cases from לולב, because לולב is special: it requires four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it can be refuted: what is special about לולב? It requires four species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other cases could not learn from לולב, because לולב has a special feature they lack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the source case has no special feature the other case lacks. לולב requires four species, so someone could say its מכשירין override שבת only because of that. Therefore the עומר and שתי הלחם could not learn from לולב and needed their own source.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted
What is special about...?
Since; because
Requires four species

phrases.english: Because it can be refuted:
what is special about lulav?
That it requires four species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא — the comparison fails because לולב has a unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Write ״ביום״ once, by לולב, and learn the rest from it
steps.terutzMaskana: לולב is too special (four species) to be the model, so the עומר and שתי הלחם need their own source

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר: סוכה and its מכשירין override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier ברייתא: according to רבי אליעזר, סוכה and all its מכשירין override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: סוכה and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a ruling of רבי אליעזר from earlier in the sugya. This sets up a search for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the subject moves from לולב to סוכה. According to רבי אליעזר, even preparations for the סוכה, like cutting wood or building it, may be done on שבת when needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The booth used on סוכות
Its preparations
Override שבת

phrases.english: Sukka and all its facilitators
override Shabbat,
the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּכָּה וְכׇל מַכְשִׁירֶיהָ דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי אליעזר's ruling about סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, סוכה and all its מכשירין override שבת.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's source for סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אליעזר learns that the מכשירין of סוכה override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רבי אליעזר know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's ruling about סוכה. The next steps test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק about סוכה says ״ביום״. So the גמרא looks for another case that רבי אליעזר might be comparing it to.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know this?

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible source and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר and שתי הלחם are offerings for the Temple service, so they have a higher standing. סוכה is a personal מצוה, so it cannot be learned from them.

The two loaves offered on שבועות
A need of the Temple service

steps.title: Not from לולב: it needs four species
steps.stepSummary: סוכה cannot be learned from לולב either, because לולב requires four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: If from לולב: it is different, because it requires four species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects a second possible source. The next step (step 21) gives רבי אליעזר's real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same special feature from Step 16 shows up again: לולב needs four species, so it cannot be a model for סוכה. With both sources rejected, the גמרא still needs to find רבי אליעזר's source.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch taken with the four species

steps.whatToRemember: Every case where מכשירין override שבת has its own special feature (Temple need, four species). That is why none of them can easily serve as the model for סוכה.

phrases.english: If from lulav —
it is different, as it requires four species.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: לולב requires four species, a special feature that סוכה lacks

steps.title: סוכה is learned from לולב through the words 'seven days'
steps.stepSummary: Since simple logic failed, the גמרא says רבי אליעזר learns סוכה from לולב through a גזירה שוה on the words 'שבעת ימים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learned 'seven days' from לולב. Just as there, by לולב, its preparations override שבת, so too here, by סוכה, its preparations override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the question from step 18. רבי אליעזר's source for סוכה is a word-link (גזירה שוה) to לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-20 showed that we cannot compare סוכה to עומר or לולב by logic, because each has a special feature. A גזירה שוה is different. It is a Torah-given link between two matching words, so it works even when the two cases are not similar. The Torah says 'seven days' by both לולב and סוכה, so the rule about preparations carries over.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned / derived (a law from another source)
'Seven days': the shared phrase used by both לולב and סוכה
Preparations that make a מצוה possible (e.g., building the סוכה)
'Just as there... so too here': the standard formula of a גזירה שוה
A Torah derivation linking two laws through a shared word or phrase

steps.confusionAlert: Don't ask, 'But סוכה and לולב are different!' The steps before this showed that differences block a logical comparison. A גזירה שוה is not a logical comparison, so the differences don't matter here.

phrases.english: Rather, he derived 'seven days' from lulav:
phrases.notes: The phrase 'seven days' appears by both לולב and סוכה in ויקרא כ״ג.

phrases.aramaic: מַה לְּהַלָּן מַכְשִׁירָיו דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From a גזירה שוה of 'שבעת ימים' linking סוכה to לולב.

steps.title: Why not write the rule by סוכה and learn everything else from it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: let the Torah state the rule about preparations by סוכה, and derive the other cases from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write it by סוכה, and let us bring these other cases and learn them from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the Torah needed a source elsewhere. It suggests that the Torah could have taught the rule by סוכה alone, and everything else could be learned from there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern the גמרא used for לולב in step 15. If one case can teach all the others, the Torah should pick that case. The challenge assumes nothing about סוכה would stop the other cases from being learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One': a name for the Torah / ה׳ as lawgiver
These (the other cases already discussed)
And let them be learned from it

phrases.english: And let the Torah write it with regard to sukka,
and let us bring these others and derive them from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for a separate source, using the same pattern as the לולב challenge in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate sources for each מצוה's preparations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If סוכה could serve as the source, the Torah should have taught the rule once there and let the other cases follow from it.

steps.title: סוכה is special: it applies at night too
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the other cases cannot be learned from סוכה, because סוכה is unique in applying both night and day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is a way to refute it: what is special about סוכה? It applies at night just as by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. סוכה has a 'stronger' feature that the other cases lack, so they cannot be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn a weaker case from a stronger case if the stronger case has no special feature. סוכה is a מצוה you keep all day and all night, while the others apply only by day. So one could argue that only סוכה's preparations override שבת, because it is such a constant מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute (by pointing out a difference between cases)
'What about X? It has a special feature': a refutation formula
Applies at night just as during the day

phrases.english: Because it can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְסוּכָּה שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֶגֶת בַּלֵּילוֹת כְּבַיָּמִים.
phrases.english: What is special about sukka? That it applies at night as during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by pointing out a unique feature of סוכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (פירכא): the proposed source has a unique stringency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everything could be learned from סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: סוכה applies night and day, so the other cases cannot be learned from it. Each needs its own source.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: מצה and its preparations override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the earlier ברייתא: according to רבי אליעזר, מצה and all its preparations override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: מצה and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the ברייתא, which is מצה. This sets up a new search for רבי אליעזר's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Preparations' of מצה means things like grinding the flour and baking the מצה. רבי אליעזר holds these may be done on שבת if they could not be done beforehand. The next step asks for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread eaten on the night of פסח
Override (push aside) the laws of שבת
The תנא who holds that מכשירי מצוה override שבת

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's source for מצה?

steps.title: Not from עומר and שתי הלחם: they are Temple needs

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible source and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עומר and שתי הלחם are offerings for the Temple service (צורך גבוה). One could argue that only such holy needs override שבת. מצה is a personal מצוה of eating, so it may be weaker.

The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

steps.title: Not from לולב: it needs four species

steps.title: מצה is learned from סוכות through the word 'fifteenth'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns מצה from סוכה through a גזירה שוה on 'חמשה עשר' (the fifteenth), which appears by both festivals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learned 'fifteenth' and 'fifteenth' from חג הסוכות. Just as there its preparations override שבת, so too here its preparations override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer to step 25. רבי אליעזר's source for מצה is a גזירה שוה linking it to סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'on the fifteenth day' both for חג המצות and for חג הסוכות. That shared word links the two, so the rule for סוכה's preparations carries over to מצה. The special feature of סוכה (night and day) doesn't block this, because a גזירה שוה does not depend on the two cases being similar.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Fifteenth': the date of both פסח and סוכות
The festival of סוכות (15th of תשרי)
The festival of מצות (15th of ניסן)

steps.whatToRemember: Pattern of this sugya: logical comparisons keep failing because each מצוה has a special feature (Temple need, four species, night and day). The real sources are גזירות שוות. סוכה comes from לולב ('seven days'), and מצה comes from סוכה ('fifteenth').
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the classic difference between a logical comparison, which any difference can break, and a גזירה שוה, which is a word-link that holds even when the cases differ.

phrases.english: so too here (matza), its facilitators override Shabbat.

steps.title: Why not write the rule by מצה and learn everything else from it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let the Torah write the rule by מצה, and let לולב and סוכה learn from מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה write it about מצה, and let those other מצוות come and learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the learning. If one source can teach the others, why not make מצה the source?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that מצה learns from סוכה through a גזירה שוה. The גמרא asks why the Torah did not do it the other way around: write the rule by מצה and let the others learn from it. That would make the extra source unnecessary.

and let them learn from it
those (the other מצוות)

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one מצוה can be the source for the others, the Torah should have written it by מצה and let the others learn from it.

steps.title: מצה is unique because it applies to women too
steps.stepSummary: מצה cannot be the source, because it has a special strength: it applies to women just as it applies to men.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we can refute it: what about מצה? It is special, since it applies to women just as to men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other מצוות could not learn from מצה, because מצה has a feature they lack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are obligated in מצה even though it is a time-bound מצוה‎. סוכה and לולב apply only to men. Because מצה has a wider obligation, one could argue that only מצה is strong enough to override שבת, so the others could not learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: to refute, to break a comparison
women
applies, is in effect

phrases.english: Because one can refute it:

That it applies to women as to men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30

steps.terutzMaskana: מצה is stronger because it applies to women, so the others cannot learn from it. That is why מצה itself is learned from סוכות through the גזירה שוה of ״חמשה עשר״ and does not serve as the source.
steps.whatToRemember: Each source מצוה has its own special feature: עומר and שתי הלחם serve the מקדש, לולב needs four species, סוכה applies day and night, and מצה applies to women.

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר learn this for שופר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's source for the rule about שופר.

steps.title: None of the earlier מצוות can be the source for שופר

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries every source we have seen so far and rejects each one.

the four species of סוכות
if (you say)

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִמַּצָּה — שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֶגֶת בַּנָּשִׁים כְּבָאֲנָשִׁים.
phrases.english: If from matza — it applies to women as to men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מֵעוֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם שֶׁכֵּן צוֹרֶךְ גָּבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible sources for the question in step 33
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: All five earlier מצוות as sources for שופר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each has a special strength that שופר lacks: Temple service, four species, nighttime obligation, or applying to women

steps.title: The פסוק says 'a day of blowing,' even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns it from the word 'יום' in 'יום תרועה יהיה לכם': it is the day of blowing even when that day is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says: 'A day of blowing it shall be for you.' 'Day' means even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אליעזר's real source: a verse about שופר itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no other מצוה can teach the rule, the גמרא finds it in the שופר verse. The word 'יום' tells us that the day is always a day of blowing, whatever day of the week it falls on, including שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse says
a day of blowing (the שופר)
even on שבת

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"A day of blowing it shall be for you."
"Day" — even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא יוֹם תְּרוּעָה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source after all the alternatives were rejected in step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'יום' in 'יום תרועה' teaches that the מצוה applies even on שבת

steps.title: Blowing the שופר is not forbidden labor anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'יום' comes to allow. It cannot be the blowing itself, because דבי שמואל taught that blowing a שופר is a skill and not a מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what is it needed? If you say it is for the blowing itself, the school of שמואל already taught: 'Do not do any work of labor.' This excludes blowing a שופר and removing bread from the oven, which are a skill and not a מלאכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions what exactly the verse allows on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing a שופר is a skill, not a forbidden מלאכה, so it does not need a verse to permit it. A verse saying 'even on שבת' would teach nothing new about the blowing itself, so it must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say
a teaching from the school of שמואל
removing bread from the oven wall
a skill, not a forbidden labor

phrases.english: And for what? If you say for the blowing,
but the school of Shmuel taught:
"Any work of labor you shall not do" —
this excludes blowing the shofar and removing bread from the oven,
which is a skill and not a labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the derivation in step 35 is needed for
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word 'יום' to allow blowing on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blowing is not a מלאכה, so no verse is needed to permit it on שבת.

steps.title: The verse is about the preparations
steps.stepSummary: The verse is needed to allow the preparations (מכשירין) of שופר on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is needed for the preparations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse allows the preparations, not the blowing itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Preparations such as carrying the שופר through a public area or cutting it into shape are real מלאכות. The word 'יום' teaches that these may be done on שבת for the מצוה. This is exactly רבי אליעזר's claim that 'all its preparations' override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: preparations that make the מצוה possible

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אליעזר's verse is about blowing the שופר on שבת. Blowing is a skill and not a מלאכה, so the verse is only needed for the preparations, which are real מלאכות.

phrases.english: Rather, it is for the preparations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the verse is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse permits the blowing itself on שבת
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse permits the preparations (מכשירין) on שבת

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree with רבי אליעזר, use the word 'יום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the word 'יום', since they do not use it to permit preparations on שבת. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah should teach something. The רבנן reject רבי אליעזר's reading, so the גמרא asks what the word 'יום' teaches according to them.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages who disagree with רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view reads the verse used in step 35

steps.title: The רבנן: blow by day, not by night
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'יום' to teach that שופר is blown by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that word to teach: by day and not at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the word to set the time of the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, 'יום' teaches when the מצוה is done, not whether it overrides שבת. So the שופר is blown only in the daytime.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for another teaching)
by day and not at night

phrases.english: That word is needed by them
to teach: by day and not at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to the רבנן, 'יום' teaches that שופר is blown by day, not at night

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר learn 'day, not night'?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר uses 'יום' for preparations on שבת, where does he learn that שופר is blown only by day?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר: from where does he learn 'by day and not at night'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question back to רבי אליעזר. He agrees that שופר is a daytime מצוה, so he needs another source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר already used the word 'יום' for the שבת rule, so he cannot also use it for the daytime rule. The גמרא asks for his other source.

keyTerms.meaning: at night

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer —
from where does he derive 'by day and not at night'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where רבי אליעזר learns the daytime rule, since he used 'יום' for something else
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי אליעזר's source that שופר is blown only by day

steps.title: Learned from the יום הכפורים שופר of the יובל year
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns it from 'ביום הכפורים תעבירו שופר', and all the שופר blowings of the seventh month learn from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'On יום הכפורים you shall sound the שופר throughout your land.' The cases learn from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אליעזר's source for the daytime rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the יובל שופר says 'ביום הכפורים', on the day of Atonement, which shows a daytime blowing. Since the שופר of ראש השנה and the שופר of יובל are both in the seventh month, they learn from each other. So ראש השנה blowing is also only by day.

keyTerms.meaning: he derives it from
the Day of Atonement (here, of the יובל year)
you shall sound the שופר
they learn from each other

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: 'יום תרועה' teaches that שופר preparations override שבת, and the daytime rule comes from the יובל verse. רבנן: 'יום' teaches only that שופר is blown by day.

phrases.english: He derives it from "On the Day of Atonement
you shall sound the shofar throughout your land,"
and they are learned from each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִבְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים תַּעֲבִירוּ שׁוֹפָר בְּכׇל אַרְצְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 40
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יובל verse 'ביום הכפורים' teaches daytime blowing, and the שופר blowings of the seventh month learn from each other
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both views agree that שופר is blown by day. They disagree only on whether the preparations override שבת.

steps.title: Why not write the rule only for שופר and learn the rest from it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: let the Torah write the מכשירין rule only by שופר, and let the other מצוות learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write it only regarding שופר, and let those other מצוות come and learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If שופר already teaches that preparations push off שבת, why does the Torah need to say it again for the other מצוות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, several מצוות each have their own source that allows their preparations on שבת. לולב and שופר each have a verse, while סוכה and מצה come through a גזירה שוה. The גמרא asks why separate sources are needed. One verse by שופר should be enough, and the rest could be learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
And let them learn from it
Those (the other מצוות)

phrases.english: And let the Torah write it regarding shofar
phrases.notes: Meaning: write it only by שופר

phrases.english: and let those others come and learn from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that שופר is established as having its own verse for מכשירין, the גמרא asks why the other verses are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate verses for each מצוה in רבי אליעזר's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source (שופר) could teach the rest by comparison, so the extra verses seem unnecessary.

steps.title: The ראש השנה שופר is unique: it brings ישראל's remembrance before ה׳
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn from the שופר of ראש השנה because it has a special quality. It brings the זכרונות of ישראל before their Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the blowing of the שופר of ראש השנה we cannot learn, because it brings the remembrances of ישראל before their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. The שופר of ראש השנה is too special to be a model for other מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning one law from another only works if the source has no special quality the others lack. The שופר of ראש השנה brings ישראל's remembrance before ה׳. So maybe only such an important מצוה pushes off שבת for its preparations. Other מצוות therefore cannot be learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blowing of the shofar
One cannot learn (derive) from it
Remembrances, Israel being remembered before ה׳
Since / because it has (a special quality)

phrases.english: From the blowing of the shofar of Rosh HaShana
one cannot derive —
since it brings in the remembrances of Israel
before their Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֵיכָּא לְמִיגְמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First half of the answer to step 42's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מה לה — pointing out a unique quality (פירכא) that blocks the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Other מצוות could learn the מכשירין rule from שופר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שופר of ראש השנה has a unique quality (זכרונות), so nothing can be learned from it.

steps.title: The יום הכפורים שופר is unique: it frees slaves and returns fields
steps.stepSummary: We also cannot learn from the שופר of יום הכפורים of the יובל year. Its blowing frees slaves and returns fields to their owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the blowing of יום הכפורים we cannot learn, as the Master said: once בית דין blows the שופר, slaves go free to their homes and fields go back to their owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows that the other kind of שופר, the one blown on יום הכפורים, is also too special to learn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שופר of יום הכפורים in the יובל year has huge legal power. The moment it is blown, slaves go free and sold fields return. Because of this unique power, it cannot serve as a model for regular מצוות. So the Torah needed separate verses for the other מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: The court
Slaves are released
Fields return to their original owners (יובל)
As the Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Both kinds of שופר have a special quality: ראש השנה brings זכרונות, and יום הכפורים frees slaves and returns fields. Because of this, the other מצוות cannot learn the מכשירין rule from שופר, and each needs its own verse.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the regular יום הכפורים blowing at the end of the fast. It is the שופר blown on יום הכפורים of the יובל (Jubilee) year, which announces freedom.

phrases.english: From the blowing of Yom Kippur
one cannot derive —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר: תָּקְעוּ בֵּית דִּין שׁוֹפָר,
phrases.english: as the Master said: once the court blew the shofar,
slaves are released to their homes
and fields return to their owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the answer, covering the other שופר blowing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מה לה — unique quality of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps we could learn from the יום הכפורים שופר instead.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יובל שופר has the unique power to free slaves and return fields, so no derivation is possible.

steps.title: Re-quoting the ברייתא: מילה and its preparations override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא: מילה and all its מכשירין push off שבת, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: מילה and all its preparations push off שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original ברייתא to examine its next part. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed the other מצוות that have verses for their preparations. Now it focuses on מילה itself, which is the main topic of the פרק. It quotes רבי אליעזר's ruling so it can ask where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (introduces a re-quote of an earlier text)
Circumcision
Its preparations (e.g., bringing the knife)
Push aside (override) שבת

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: מִילָה וְכׇל מַכְשִׁירֶיהָ דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Circumcision and all its preparations override Shabbat,
the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִילָה וְכׇל מַכְשִׁירֶיהָ דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the side discussion about the other מצוות and returns to the ברייתא's main ruling about מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, מילה and all its מכשירין override שבת.

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's source that the מכשירין of מילה push off שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רבי אליעזר know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's rule about מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the other מצוות had its own source, either a verse or a גזירה שוה. Now the גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר's source is for מילה, and it will first test whether מילה can be learned from those other מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know (source request)

phrases.english: From where does Rabbi Eliezer know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural or logical source for רבי אליעזר's view on the מכשירין of מילה.

steps.title: Learning מילה from all the other מצוות fails
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר learns מילה from all the other מצוות together, that fails, as already shown. A further objection, 'ועוד: מה להנך', then begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learns it from all of them, it can be refuted as we said. And furthermore: what about these (other מצוות)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible source and shoots it down. It then begins a second objection that continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might learn מילה from all the earlier מצוות put together. But the גמרא already showed that each of them has its own special quality. So none of them, even together, is a safe model. The words 'ועוד: מה להנך' open a second objection that continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If he learns it from all of them
As we have (already) said
And furthermore (adds another objection)
What is it about these (opens a 'unique quality' refutation)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence 'מה להנך' is cut off here. The rest of the objection comes on the next amud, so do not look for its ending yet.

phrases.english: If he learns it from all of them —
it is refuted as we said.
phrases.notes: Each source has its own unique quality.

phrases.english: And furthermore: what about these (מצוות)...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to step 46 and rejects it, then begins a further objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: Deriving the מכשירין of מילה from the other מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each source מצוה has its own unique quality, so even all of them together cannot serve as a model. A further distinction between those מצוות and מילה is then introduced with 'ועוד'.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the מכשירין of מילה from all the other מצוות together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each of those מצוות has its own unique quality (as already shown), so they cannot serve as a model. A further distinction is introduced with ״ועוד: מה להנך״.
